Historically, [MuddyWater](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0069) has used PowerShell-based tools and [RustyWater](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9037) reflects a shift in tooling, demonstrating better techniques for defense evasion and reverse engineering.

S9038.name: DynoWiper
S9038.description: [DynoWiper](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9038) is a destructive malware associated with the [2025 Poland Wiper Attacks](https://attack.mitre.org/campaigns/C0063) in December of 2025. [DynoWiper](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9038) is a native Windows binary that is distributed by a PowerShell script and overwrites files using data generated by the Mersenne Twister algorithm before they are deleted from the system. Multiple variants of [DynoWiper](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9038) have been identified, with the primary differences being that one variant shuts down the system after completing its destructive operations, and another introduces a time delay between file overwriting and deletion.

S9039.name: LazyWiper
S9039.description: [LazyWiper](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9039) is a destructive malware observed targeting a manufacturing sector company during the [2025 Poland Wiper Attacks](https://attack.mitre.org/campaigns/C0063). [LazyWiper](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9039) is a native Windows PowerShell script that is believed to have been generated by a large language model (LLM). [LazyWiper](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9039) overwrites files on the system using the C# function `WriteRandomBytes()` and can target multiple specific file types by their extensions.

S9041.name: TeamPCP Cloud Stealer
S9041.description: The [TeamPCP Cloud Stealer](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9041) is a comprehensive filesystem credential stealer that can harvest, encrypt, and exfiltrate credentials from over 50 sensitive file paths across CI/CD, cloud, developer tooling, and container environments. The [TeamPCP Cloud Stealer](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9041) was the primary payload used by [TeamPCP](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1056) in March 2026 during early stages of a cascading supply chain campaign targeting CI/CD workflows.

S9042.name: CanisterWorm
S9042.description: [CanisterWorm](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9042) is a self-propagating malware that has been used by [TeamPCP](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1056) in credential harvesting and software supply chain campaigns since at least 2026. [CanisterWorm](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9042) has used npm credentials to infect software packages and propagate across developer ecosystems. [CanisterWorm](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9042) has a targeted wiper component and can use decentralized C2 infrastructure implemented via an Internet Computer Protocol (ICP) blockchain canister.

S9043.name: Mini Shai-Hulud
S9043.description: [Mini Shai-Hulud](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9043) is a credential stealer and self-replicating supply chain worm, derived from [Shai-Hulud](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9008), that has been used by [TeamPCP](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1056) to target Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery/Deployment (CI/CD) workflows since at least 2026. [Mini Shai-Hulud](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9043) can compromise credentials across multiple cloud, container, and AI configuration file paths and can use stolen npm and GitHub OIDC tokens to spread to other packages maintained by the compromised user. [Mini Shai-Hulud](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9043) also has a targeted wiper component and has used multiple C2 and data exfiltration mechanisms.

S9044.name: Kali365
S9044.description: [Kali365](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9044) is a Phishing-as-a-Service (PHaaS) kit first observed in April 2026 that generates victim-targeted lures across multiple operating systems to induce users into copying and pasting actor-controlled commands for local execution. [Kali365](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9044) incorporates on-demand device code generation and mirrors the copy-paste execution tradecraft associated with ClickFix. Operators have used [Kali365](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9044) to harvest victims' OAuth tokens and session cookies through adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM) interception, enabling account takeover. [Kali365](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9044) PHaaS was first observed in April 2026. [Kali365](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9044) has also been affiliated with other branding to include Octopi365 and Freedom365.

S9045.name: BACKUPOSINT v9.0 APEX PREDATOR
S9045.description: [BACKUPOSINT v9.0 APEX PREDATOR](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9045) is a 49-module Python malware developed entirely by Anthropic’s Claude Code as part of the [AI-Assisted Breach of Mexico's Government Infrastructure](https://attack.mitre.org/campaigns/C0064) campaign. [BACKUPOSINT v9.0 APEX PREDATOR](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9045) leverages publicly available techniques for network enumeration, credential harvesting, Active Directory interrogation, database access, privilege escalation, cloud metadata extraction, and lateral movement .

S9046.name: IOControl
S9046.description: IOControl is a malware that targeted Linux ARM-based IoT/OT devices including Hikvision IP cameras, D-Link firewalls and routers, Unitronics PLCs and HMIs, Orpak and Gasboy fuel management systems, and Baicells LTE controllers across the United States and Israel. The malware has been attributed to [CyberAv3ngers](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1027) which is suspected to be affiliated with the Iranian Government Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).

S9050.name: Vidar
S9050.description: [Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) is a Windows infostealer that was first advertised in November 2018. Written in C++, [Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) collects PII, cryptocurrency wallets, documents and other data within the compromised machine. Version 2 of [Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) was published in October 2025, and has been used in numerous operations since its release. [Vidar](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9050) has been observed alongside other malware strains, including STOP/Djvu ransomware, Mina.exe (an XMRIG miner), and Clip1.exe (a Laplas Clipper sample).

S9051.name: The Gentlemen Ransomware
S9051.description: [The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) is a ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS). [The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has been written in Go programming language and has utilized Garble to obfuscate its code to target Windows environments. [The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) is capable of executing its’ OS lockers in Windows, Linux, NAS, BSD and ESXi environments. [The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) was first observed in mid-2025 as a closed ransomware and shortly later emerged as a RaaS to affiliates in September 2025. [The Gentlemen Ransomware](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9051) has been affiliated with the threat group [The Gentlemen](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1058).

S9052.name: MiniFast
S9052.description: [MiniFast](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9052) is a custom malware designed for long-term persistence and remote code execution. [MiniFast](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9052) is a modular malware suspected of being generated using artificial intelligence (AI). [MiniFast](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9052) was first observed in early-2026 and is a modified version of the [MiniJunk](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9053) framework. [MiniFast](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9052) has been affiliated with the cyber espionage threat group [NIMBUS MANTICORE](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1059).

S9053.name: MiniJunk
S9053.description: [MiniJunk](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9053) is a custom malware designed for long-term persistence and remote code execution. [MiniJunk](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9053)  was first observed in 2025 and is a modified version of the [MiniBike](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9059) framework that was first observed in June 2022. [MiniJunk](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9053) has been affiliated with the cyber espionage threat group [NIMBUS MANTICORE](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1059).

S9057.name: CRASHPAD
S9057.description: [CRASHPAD](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9057) is a Windows executable written in C++ that gathers data from web browsers. [CRASHPAD](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9057)  was first observed in 2025 and has been affiliated with the cyber espionage threat group [NIMBUS MANTICORE](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1059).

S9058.name: SIGHTGRAB
S9058.description: [SIGHTGRAB](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9058) is a Windows executable written in C that captures and stages stolen data on victim devices. [SIGHTGRAB](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9058) was first observed in 2025 and has been affiliated with the cyber espionage threat group [NIMBUS MANTICORE](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1059).

S9059.name: MiniBike
S9059.description: [MiniBike](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9059) is a custom backdoor written in C++ designed for command execution, data discovery, gathering, and exfiltration. [MiniBike](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9059) has been known to communicate with the C2 using Azure Cloud Infrastructure. [MiniBike](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9059) was first observed in 2022. [MiniBike](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9059) has been affiliated with the cyber espionage threat group [NIMBUS MANTICORE](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1059).

S9060.name: MiniBus
S9060.description: [MiniBus](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9060) is a custom backdoor used for command execution, data discovery, gathering, and exfiltration. [MiniBus](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9060) has utilized Azure Cloud Infrastructure and unique adversary-controlled domains for command and control. [MiniBus](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9060) is an updated platform to its predecessor [MiniBike](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9059) and was first observed in August 2023. [MiniBus](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9060) has been affiliated with the cyber espionage threat group [NIMBUS MANTICORE](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1059).

S9061.name: LIGHTRAIL
S9061.description: [LIGHTRAIL](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9061) is a tunneler malware. [LIGHTRAIL](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9061) has been known to communicate with C2 SOCKS4A Websocket communications. [LIGHTRAIL](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9061) was first observed in 2022. [LIGHTRAIL](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9061) has been affiliated with the cyber espionage threat group [NIMBUS MANTICORE](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1059).

S9062.name: MiniBrowse
S9062.description: [MiniBrowse](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9062) is a custom stealer designed for the theft of credentials in browsers and passwords stores. [MiniBrowse](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9062) was first observed in late-2025. [MiniBrowse](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9062) has been affiliated with the cyber espionage threat group [NIMBUS MANTICORE](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1059).

S9063.name: DEEPROOT
S9063.description: [DEEPROOT](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9063) is a Linux backdoor written in Golang. [DEEPROOT](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9063) is able to execute commands via a shell, enumerate systems, delete or download files, and exfiltrate data. [DEEPROOT](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9063) was first observed in 2025. [DEEPROOT](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9063) has been affiliated with the cyber espionage threat group [NIMBUS MANTICORE](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1059).

S9064.name: TRUSTTRAP
S9064.description: [TRUSTTRAP](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9064) is a malware that uses a fictitious prompt to trick users to submit their credentials. [TRUSTTRAP](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9064) was first observed in 2023 and has been affiliated with the cyber espionage threat group [NIMBUS MANTICORE](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1059).

S9065.name: DCSYNCER.SLICK
S9065.description: [DCSYNCER.SLICK](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9065) is a Windows executable that is designed to gather credentials from victim devices. [DCSYNCER.SLICK](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9065) was first observed in 2025 and has been affiliated with the cyber espionage threat group [NIMBUS MANTICORE](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1059).

S9066.name: POLLBLEND
S9066.description: [POLLBLEND](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9066) is a Windows tunneler written C++ that has utilized hardcoded C2 servers and leveraged hardcoded URI parameters for follow-on actions. [POLLBLEND](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9066) was first observed in 2025 and has been affiliated with the cyber espionage threat group [NIMBUS MANTICORE](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1059).

S9067.name: TWOSTROKE
S9067.description: [TWOSTROKE](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9067) is malicious backdoor written in C++ that is capable of discovery actions, executing payloads and exfiltrating data. [TWOSTROKE](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9067) was first observed in 2025 and has been affiliated with the cyber espionage threat group [NIMBUS MANTICORE](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1059).
